title: Introduce entropy-driven load reshaper and kernel-signature reporter
author: Sana Iqbal
description:
Motivation: existing synthetic workload generators focus on sequence length and burstiness but ignore token-level entropy patterns that materially change generation branching and effective kernel choices. This PR adds an entropy-driven load reshaper that synthesizes request streams guided by token entropy distributions, plus a kernel-signature reporter that correlates observed kernel selection (quantized vs fp16 paths, attention kernel variants) with entropy and priming patterns. The goal is to surface cases where high-entropy prompts force different kernels and produce tail latency regressions not visible in current baselines.

What this change does: Implements a new workload runner (entropy_resampler) that consumes token-level entropy histograms or a fitted generative model to produce a time-series of requests with configurable entropy drift, local spikes, and sequence-length coupling. Adds an offline kernel-signature reporter that attaches lightweight per-request metadata (predicted kernel variant, observed kernel id from the runtime shim, kv-cache hit ratio, effective batch size) to existing flamepoint traces and exports a compact summary CSV/Parquet for analysis. Integrates the runner into the benchmark orchestration with new CLI flags and adds e2e integration tests that validate statistical properties (entropy distribution matching, burst ratio, and replication determinism with seed).

Why it matters: Several perf regressions in November were traced to model inputs with unusually high per-token entropy that changed micro-kernel selection under contention; these regressions were not reproducible with our sequence-length-based generators. This tooling provides a repeatable way to exercise that axis and ties kernel telemetry back to the workload signals engineers care about.

Compatibility & safety: The new reporter subscribes to existing telemetry hooks and uses the same privacy-preserving scrubbing pipeline (hashing prompt prefixes) — no plaintext model inputs are exported. The runner has a conservative default profile aimed at non-destructive load testing.

Usage notes: "benchctl run entropy-resampler --profile drift_high --duration 15m --out report.parquet" will produce both the trace augmentation and the kernel-signature report. Example notebooks (notebooks/entropy-analysis.ipynb) show how to join the report with flamegraphs and trace logs for root-cause analysis.

Migration & rollout: Feature is gated behind --experimental-entropies flag and a config toggle in the benchmark lab main pipeline. We plan to enable it in nightly perf runs for two weeks before promoting to weekly baselines.
commit_summary: 4 commits: (1) add entropy_resampler runner and CLI integration; (2) implement kernel-signature reporter and exporter; (3) telemetry adapter and privacy scrubbing hooks; (4) tests, docs, and example notebook
review_comments: Marco Alvarez: Can you add a short note in the docs about the privacy guarantees and which fields are hashed?
Sana Iqbal: Added detailed scrubbing section and an integration test that validates no raw prompts are written to disk.
Priya Nair: The default profile seems a bit aggressive for CI. Suggest lowering concurrency and adding a quick smoke profile for presubmit runs.
Sana Iqbal: Added 'ci_smoke' template and changed the nightly job to use it by default when --ci flag is set.
Jonas Keller: Nice telemetry mapping. Can we also emit a compact per-kernel latency histogram?
Sana Iqbal: Added optional histogram output (kernel_histograms.parquet) behind --emit-kernel-hist flag.
release_notes: Introduce entropy-driven workload generator (entropy_resampler) and kernel-signature reporter. Enables correlation of token-entropy patterns with selected runtime kernels and tail latency. Experimental feature behind feature-flag; nightly baseline enabled.
